voyage.name: Bratislava Castle
voyage.content: The castle contains a Museum of Bratislava History, and a baroque garden. There is also a restaurant open till after the actual castle tours into the night. The general precinct area immediately outside the castle, including the vantage points of the city are usually always open during the daytime, and is free to access.

voyage.name: Slovak National Gallery (SNG)
voyage.content: For a taste of visual arts, pay a visit to the National Gallery at the embankment between Starý most and Nový most with permanent collections of Slovak and European medieval art pieces, although the temporary exhibitions tend to be far more interesting.

voyage.name: Bratislava City Gallery (GMB)
voyage.content: Bratislava City Gallery is also a good pick to see displays of historical fine arts, paintings and sculptures along with interesting temporary exhibitions.

voyage.name: Danubiana Meulensteen Art Museum
voyage.content: If you like modern art better, pay a visit to the Danubiana Art Museum on the southern edge of Bratislava. It is about 20km from the city center, so too far to walk. Take bus nr 90 from the National Theater, a taxi, or drive. It is located on the Gabčíkovo Dam, a hydroelectric power plant.

voyage.name: Milan Dobes Museum
voyage.content: This small museum features modernist Op-art. It lies in the city center and is recommended to all interested in the development of modern art.

voyage.name: National Museum
voyage.content: Permanent archaelogical collections.

voyage.name: Natural Science Museum
voyage.content: Echoing the communist era, the natural science exhibitions have an interesting collection of artifacts and is slowly being transformed into a modern era exhibition.

voyage.name: Gerulata
voyage.content: This is an ancient Roman military camp with archeological findings on display. If you're into all things Roman, you should also consider a visit to the nearby Carnuntum which has a large archeological site and is a few minutes by car from Bratislava.

voyage.name: Museum of Transport
voyage.price: Adults €8, students and seniors 65-70 €4, children 3-6 and seniors 70+ €1, children under 3 free. Free entry on first Wednesday of each month
voyage.content: With a display of historical vehicles (automobiles, farm vehicles, bicycles, firefighting vehicles, railway, model ships and model buses) in the first railway station in the city, very close to the current Main Railway Station. Free parking in front of the museum for up to 4 hours by displaying the ticket on the dashboard.

voyage.name: Museum of Trade
voyage.content: This museum has some remarking pieces of historic advertising plates and other artifacts.

voyage.name: Jewish Community Museum
voyage.content: Rare Jewish ritual tools, gold-embroidered mantles protecting the holy biblical scrolls, unique photographs of students who had attended the famed Bratislava rabbi school that reveal even to this day the atrocities of the Holocaust. It is situated in the Heydukova Street Synagogue, which is the only synagogue in Bratislava. Constructed in 1923-1926, it is a Cubist building designed by the Bratislava-based Jewish arch

voyage.name: Museum of City History
voyage.content: Including the museums of history and music as well as the city dungeon and the exhibition on medieval justice.

voyage.name: Devín Castle
voyage.price: €8 April to October, €6 November to March
voyage.content: There has been a fortress on this site since Roman times. In the 19th and early 20th century it became a Slovak national symbol. During the Communist dictatorship, it was part of the border zone which prevented people from escaping the country.

voyage.name: St. Martin's Cathedral
voyage.content: The largest and one of the oldest churches in Bratislava, situated below Bratislava Castle. The Gothic cathedral, formerly the coronation-church of several Hungarian kings, begun in 1204, and reconsecrated in 1445, was restored in 1861-80. The tower is surmounted by a pyramid bearing a gilded Hungarian royal crown.

voyage.name: St. Clare's Church
voyage.content: A Gothic church on Klariská street, in the historical center; now used as a concert hall.

voyage.name: Church of St. Elisabeth
voyage.content: Nicknamed the Blue Church (Modrý kostolík), this is a beautiful Jugendstil church finished in 1913.

voyage.name: Primate's Palace
voyage.content: Now the seat of the Mayor of Bratislava.

voyage.name: Old Town Hall
voyage.content: The Old Town Hall and Apponyi Palace is open to the public as a museum, with an exhibition of city history.

voyage.name: Grassalkovich Palace and gardens
voyage.content: Also known as the Presidential Palace (Prezidentský palác) - a Rococo/late Baroque summer palace with a French garden, used as a seat of the President of Slovakia. In one of the garden's alleys you will see a row of trees planted by famous people such as Juan Carlos I (King of Spain). In front of the Palace you will see the Slovak National Guard.

voyage.name: Gallery Nedbalka
voyage.content: Gallery of modern Slovak art from the late 19th century, in a building reminiscent of the New York Guggenheim.

voyage.name: Mirbach Palace
voyage.content: Rococo Palace built 1768–1770. Today it hosts the Bratislava City Gallery.

voyage.name: Palffy Palace
voyage.content: Rebuilt in the classical style in the 19th century by Count John Pálffy. Part of the Bratislava City Gallery.

voyage.name: Academia Istropolitana
voyage.content: The oldest historic university in the area, which is now occupied by the state of Slovakia, from the 13th century.

voyage.name: Slovak National Theatre
voyage.content: The historic building of the Slovak National Theatre, built in 1886.

voyage.name: Slovak Radio Building
voyage.content: Its main building is a peculiar 60-m-high reversed pyramid from the communist era and a landmark in sharp contrast with the building of the Slovak National Bank just across the street.

voyage.name: Slavín monument
voyage.content: On the top of the hill behind the castle, overlooking the entire city. This is a monument in memory of Soviet casualties in the liberation battle of Bratislava in World War II. It is the highest place in the city, and thus the best place for viewing the city. Slavin is a cemetery and thus rather quiet. On warm nights it's a very romantic place, allowing you to sit in the shadows of the monument and look at the traffi

voyage.name: Roland Fountain
voyage.content: Built by stone cutter Andreas Luttringer and commissioned by Hungarian king Maximilian in 1527, this was the first fountain in Bratislava.

voyage.name: Michael's Gate with Tower
voyage.content: This 51-m-high tower above the gate with its green copper roof is one of the best known and the oldest buildings in Bratislava. It was built in the 14th century as one of the four gates to the city.

voyage.name: Jewish Cemetery, Jewish Community Museum and Bratislava Synagogue
voyage.content: The only synagogue in Bratislava.

voyage.name: SNP Bridge
voyage.alt: Most Slovenského národného povstania, called Nový most from 1993 to 2012
voyage.price: Entrance €6.50, but is free of charge if you eat in the restaurant
voyage.content: A bridge over the Danube river, with its flying saucer-shaped structure housing a restaurant called "UFO". There is an observation deck on its roof, open from 10:00-23:00 daily, offering great views of the old town, as well as the apartment blocks in Petržalka.

voyage.name: Bratislava Card
voyage.price: With unlimited public transportation: €30 for 24 hr, €36 for 48 hr, €39 for 72 hr. Without public transportation: €27 for 24 hr, €32 for 48 hr, €35 for 72 hr
voyage.content: This is very good value, particularly if visiting for more than 24 hours. You can purchase either a physical or digital card. Available for 24, 48 or 72 hrs. Time starts when you first use the physical card or activates the digital card in its app and expires at the end of the purchased duration (not calendar day). Includes free guided downtown walking tour. Free access to 23 museums and galleries around Bratislava r

voyage.name: Speedboats.sk
voyage.content: Enjoy the beautiful view of Bratislava and the surrounding nature of the river Danube during a Bratislava boat trip.

voyage.name: International Film Festival Bratislava
voyage.content: Forever in December.

voyage.name: The Uprising Music Festival
voyage.content: Smaller multigenre music festival. Yearly in the end of August in Bratislava.

voyage.name: Góvinda reštaurácia
voyage.content: Hare Krishna-operated restaurant popular with vegans and very affordable.

voyage.name: KGB Krčma Gurmánov Bratislavy
voyage.content: Communism-themed pub with high-quality beers and affordable prices.

voyage.name: U Sedliaka
voyage.content: Good typical Slovak dishes and great background music. Nice atmosphere at affordable price.

voyage.name: Olive Tree
voyage.content: Good selection of Slovac cuisine

voyage.name: Divný Janko Reštaurácia
voyage.content: Slovak and international dishes in a nice, retro ambience, the only downside is that the staff can be rude.

voyage.name: Slovak Pub
voyage.content: For good and reasonably priced halušky, the unique Slovak national meal, visit the Slovak Pub on Obchodna. This is a traditional eatery with a nice ambience. Portion size leans towards the small side. Not wheelchair accessible.

voyage.name: Flagship
voyage.content: Slovak national cuisine including halušky, in a converted theatre. Lacklustre service. Same company as Slovak Pub, who also own brewery Kláštorný pivovar, and café Franz Xaver Messerschmidt next door.

voyage.name: San Marten
voyage.content: San Marten is an Italian restaurant with great food and excellent service at affordable prices.

voyage.name: Bistro SOHO
voyage.content: Asian fusion cuisine.

voyage.name: Mille Baci
voyage.content: Italian restaurant specializing in dishes from Veneto.

voyage.name: UFO
voyage.content: You can get a nice view and can meet some local celebrities at the übercool and very expensive UFO restaurant and disco on top of Nový most bridge.

voyage.name: ECK
voyage.content: Regarded as one of the best restaurants in Slovakia, bookings open two months in advance and sell out almost immediately.

voyage.name: UFO
voyage.content: If you want to go for extraordinary, visit UFO. It looks like a cliché flying saucer and it's a high on the SNP Bridge (the member of great-towers.com), and you have to use a lift to go there. There is a good restaurant and lounge bar and observation deck. The view is incomparable.

voyage.name: ruido.cafe
voyage.content: Gay bar.

voyage.name: Apollon Gay Club
voyage.content: Gay bar.

voyage.name: Patio Hostel
voyage.content: Very popular, in the centre, close to the train & bus stations, easily reachable from the airport. Dorms and privates, free Internet, parking lot, laundry.

voyage.name: Wild Elephants Hostel
voyage.content: Accommodations available for people aged 18-40 years old only.

voyage.name: Hotel Arcus
voyage.content: Nice family hotel, big rooms and bathrooms, fresh cooked breakfast.

voyage.name: Boutique Apartments Possonium
voyage.content: Only 3 minutes by walk from Hlavna stanica (main railway station). Free breakfast, Wi-Fi, internet, free laundry, cosy bar, great chill out in the garden.

voyage.name: Downtown Bratislava Hotel
voyage.content: 18 minutes' walk from the central station.

voyage.name: Hotel Ibis
voyage.content: Double rooms from €48, in central location, just a short walk from the Old town.

voyage.name: Mercure Bratislava Centrum Hotel
voyage.content: Mid-scale business hotel (with aggressively modern decorations), a short walk from the main railway station. About 15–20 minutes’ walk from the old town, with frequent trams and buses available. Rate includes wired and wireless Internet access.

voyage.name: Saffron Hotel
voyage.content: Business Hotel, walking distance to the old town, or a 10 minute tram. Parking available for €12/day. Superb gym, which unfortunately is only open 10am–10pm.

voyage.name: Albrecht
voyage.content: Design hotel with 12 rooms and suites nestled on hill above Bratislava castle and Old Town. The Albrecht features flagship restaurant and lounge bar as well as lavish urban spa - unique in Bratislava.

voyage.name: Arcadia
voyage.content: Boutique hotel with heritage-style decor.

voyage.name: Devín
voyage.content: Traditional hotel with 100 rooms and suites in the historical centre of Bratislava, walking distance to all main attraction. It provides accommodation, restaurant, conference services and relaxation center with pool.

voyage.name: Gate One
voyage.content: Business and conference hotel near airport.

voyage.name: Kempinski Hotel River Park
voyage.content: Directly overlooking the Danube.

voyage.name: Park Inn by Radisson Danube Bratislava
voyage.content: Central location.

voyage.name: Perugia
voyage.content: Near the main square.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Carlton Hotel, Bratislava
voyage.content: In the heart of Bratislava, it has been fully renovated and retains many of its original features.

voyage.name: Sheraton Bratislava Hotel
voyage.content: In Bratislava's sophisticated new city center EUROVEA, the first Sheraton hotel in Slovakia offers 186 stylish guest rooms and 23 suites and Shine Spa - wellness center with indoor swimming pool, saunas, 24/7 gym and many different massages.

voyage.name: Falkensteiner Bratislava Hotel
voyage.content: Close to city centre, business hotel.

voyage.name: Beigli Hotel & Garden
voyage.content: In the city center - no car access.

voyage.name: Hotel Hradná Brána
voyage.content: First class hotel has a panoramic view over the Devín castle. It provides accommodation, restaurant, congressional and relaxation services.
